fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. "When the wine ran out…" is how the writer puts it. I think a wedding running out of wine is a rough spot, and I've had a cookie jar echo at me before. Sad sound.
Simon Peter was one of the men Jesus called as disciples (John 1:40-42), so it's a fair guess. But the one who says it is Jesus' mother: "They have no more wine." She's the one who brings it to Him.

Nathanael is another man who came to Jesus earlier in John (John 1:45-49), so I see why he came to mind. This passage doesn't record him saying anything. Jesus' mother is the one who tells Him, "They have no more wine."
The text doesn't show her sitting back down. She turns to the servants and says, "Do whatever He tells you." She keeps moving after Jesus' answer.
Right, baker. Jesus tells the servants, "Fill the jars with water." Water, in jars that had been set there for the Jewish rites of purification.
Yes, it's false. The text says, "So they filled them to the brim." Six jars, each able to hold from twenty to thirty gallons, all filled to the top.
That's right. The master of the banquet "…did not know where it was from…" He just tastes it and gets to be impressed. The text says the servants who had drawn the water knew.
Yes, baker. The text says "…the servants who had drawn the water knew." They drew the water, and they knew where it was from. I'd love to have seen their faces.
The disciples are at the wedding, but the text doesn't say they drew the water. It says "…the servants who had drawn the water knew." The ones who drew the water are the ones who knew.

Guests are a fair guess, baker. The text says the servants who had drawn the water knew where the wine came from. The master of the banquet didn't know, and the text doesn't say the guests did either.
True, baker. The text says Jesus revealed His glory, "…and His disciples believed in Him." This is called the first of His signs. Their belief is right there in the verse.
Not false, baker. The text says Jesus "…revealed His glory, and His disciples believed in Him." That's said about the first of His signs at Cana. So the answer is True.
